diagnostics.message:
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.google_project_iam_binding.authoritative` mutates the project IAM policy (cloudresourcemanager/IAM APIs) but is only ordered after `:resource.google_project.project`. `:resource.google_project_service.project_services` enables those APIs asynchronously and sets `disable_on_destroy`/`disable_dependent_services`, so on create the roles granted here may refer to services that are not yet enabled, and on destroy the policy binding is removed in parallel with the APIs being disabled — the same failure mode the module already guards against on `google_compute_project_metadata_item.oslogin_meta`. It should depend on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services` (bare `depends_on`; no attribute here can reference the service resources).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`google_project_iam_binding.authoritative` only depends on `google_project.project` (via `project = google_project.project.project_id`); nothing orders it after `google_project_service.project_services`. Setting authoritative bindings requires the project's IAM/Cloud Resource Manager APIs to be live, and on destroy the module disables services (`disable_on_destroy = true`, `disable_dependent_services = true`), so removing bindings after the APIs are torn down fails. This is the same ordering the module already encodes for `google_compute_project_metadata_item.oslogin_meta` ("depend on services or it will fail on destroy"). Add `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`:resource.google_project_iam_binding.authoritative` only references `google_project.project`, so it can be applied before the APIs in `var.services` are enabled. The members it binds often include service agents that are created only when their API is enabled (e.g. `<project_number>@cloudservices.gserviceaccount.com`), and disabling services on destroy with surviving bindings can error. It should depend on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services` (e.g. via depends_on, as already done for `google_compute_project_metadata_item.oslogin_meta`).

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.google_project_iam_custom_role.roles` creates custom roles whose `permissions` belong to services this module enables, but has no ordering against `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`. Custom role creation validates the permission set against enabled services, so it can fail if the backing API has not finished enabling; on destroy it is likewise torn down in parallel with `disable_on_destroy` disabling those APIs. Add a `depends_on` on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`google_project_iam_custom_role.roles` depends only on `google_project.project`; it is not ordered after `google_project_service.project_services`. Custom roles carry permissions belonging to the APIs enabled by that resource, so role creation/validation and especially destroy-time deletion can race with service enable/disable. Add `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.google_project_iam_member.additive` writes additive IAM members via the IAM/cloudresourcemanager APIs, but only depends on `:resource.google_project.project`. It is not ordered against `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`, so granting roles provided by services that are still being enabled can fail, and on destroy the memberships are removed concurrently with `disable_on_destroy` disabling the APIs they rely on. Add an explicit `depends_on` on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`google_project_iam_member.additive` depends only on `google_project.project`; nothing orders it after `google_project_service.project_services`. Non-authoritative IAM writes are read-modify-write on the project IAM policy and can fail (or be reverted) when they race a service being enabled/disabled, and the module disables dependent services on destroy. Add `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`:resource.google_project_iam_member.additive` grants roles to members supplied by the caller, which commonly include per-service service accounts (cloudservices, container-engine-robot, containerregistry, appspot, etc.) that only exist after `:resource.google_project_service.project_services` enables the corresponding APIs. Without that ordering the binding fails with "service account does not exist".

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.google_project_iam_member.oslogin_iam_serviceaccountuser` grants `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`, which requires the IAM API to be enabled, yet it has no ordering against `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`. Creation can race the asynchronous API enablement and destruction races `disable_on_destroy`. Add `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`google_project_iam_member.oslogin_iam_serviceaccountuser` grants `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` but only depends on `google_project.project`; nothing orders it after `google_project_service.project_services`. As with the other OS Login grants in this module, the IAM write can race service enable/disable (the module disables dependent services on destroy). Add `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`:resource.google_project_iam_member.oslogin_iam_serviceaccountuser` grants `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` to OS Login admins/users but does not depend on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`; it should be applied after service enablement (and after the service agents those members reference exist).

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.google_project_iam_member.oslogin_compute_viewer` grants `roles/compute.viewer`, which is only valid once the Compute API is enabled, but it is not ordered after `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`. Both the grant and (on destroy) the removal can race the project's service enable/disable lifecycle. Add an explicit `depends_on` on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`google_project_iam_member.oslogin_compute_viewer` grants `roles/compute.viewer` but depends only on `google_project.project`; it is not ordered after `google_project_service.project_services`, which enables the Compute API. The grant can be applied before the API exists and can be torn down after it is disabled. Add `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`:resource.google_project_iam_member.oslogin_compute_viewer` grants `roles/compute.viewer` without any ordering against `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`, so it can race service enablement on a freshly created project.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.google_project_iam_member.oslogin_admins` grants `roles/compute.osAdminLogin`, a Compute-API-provided role, with no dependency on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`. It can be applied before the Compute API has finished enabling and is removed in parallel with `disable_on_destroy` disabling it. Add a `depends_on` on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`google_project_iam_member.oslogin_admins` grants `roles/compute.osAdminLogin` but only depends on `google_project.project`; it is not ordered after `google_project_service.project_services`, which enables the Compute API these OS Login roles belong to. Granting them before the service is enabled (and removing them after it is disabled, given `disable_dependent_services = true`) can fail. Add `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`:resource.google_project_iam_member.oslogin_admins` grants `roles/compute.osAdminLogin` on a new project but only depends on `google_project.project`, so it can run before `:resource.google_project_service.project_services` enables the Compute API. Granting service-specific roles / service-agent members before the API exists fails, so it should be ordered after service enablement.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.google_project_iam_member.oslogin_users` grants `roles/compute.osLogin`, a Compute-API-provided role, with no dependency on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`. As with `google_compute_project_metadata_item.oslogin_meta`, the OS Login / Compute API ordering matters on both apply and destroy. Add `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`google_project_iam_member.oslogin_users` grants `roles/compute.osLogin` but only depends on `google_project.project`; nothing orders it after `google_project_service.project_services`, the resource that enables the Compute API backing that role. This races service enable on create and service disable on destroy. Add `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`:resource.google_project_iam_member.oslogin_users` grants `roles/compute.osLogin` but is not ordered after `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`, so it may be applied before the Compute API is enabled; bindings referencing service roles/agents can fail in that window.
